title: River Review Completion Assessment
description: Evidence-based DONE proof for one review run (#2019, Epic #2011 Phase 8). `claimed complete != proven complete`: this document records whether the evidence supports a completion claim, NOT whether the loop may advance. Completion and Gate are separate contracts (Epic #2011 invariant I6): the gate vocabulary (GATE_DECISIONS / GATE_REASON_CODES in `src/lib/gate-decision.mjs`) answers "should the host proceed", this document answers "is the goal / requirement / acceptance-criterion evidence in place". The two vocabularies are disjoint by construction and `tests/completion-assessment.test.mjs` imports the gate ledger and pins the disjointness, so neither side can absorb the other. This document carries NO merge, release or approval field: a completion state MUST NOT be wired to merge authority, and business-value judgment is returned to a human via `HUMAN_JUDGMENT_REQUIRED`. `mode` is `observe` only, so an assessment cannot alter an existing decision, gate or finding. Vocabulary is closed: every enum is closed and every object sets `additionalProperties: false`, so an unknown state fails validation instead of degrading silently — the same fail-safe direction recorded in `src/lib/gate-decision.mjs`.

schemaVersion.description: Version of THIS document shape (artifact schemaVersion, not an asset version).

mode.description: Only `observe` exists in #2019. An assessment is recorded alongside the existing outputs and MUST NOT change an existing decision, gate or finding. Adding an enforcing mode is therefore a schema change (a reviewable event), not a field flip.

reasonCodes.description: Why the state is what it is. Disjoint from GATE_REASON_CODES by construction; `tests/completion-assessment.test.mjs` pins that against the imported gate ledger.

verification.description: Verification = did the change satisfy the REQUIREMENTS that were defined. Distinct from `validation`, which asks whether the original GOAL was achieved. Splitting the two is a #2019 requirement: a run can satisfy every stated requirement and still fail the goal.

validation.description: Validation = can the ORIGINAL GOAL be called achieved. Meaningful only at `final` scope: a single task has no goal of its own to validate, which is why `scope: task` forbids this property outright rather than allowing an empty one. When the answer needs a business or value judgment, `state` is `REQUIRES_HUMAN_JUDGMENT` and the document's own `state` becomes `HUMAN_JUDGMENT_REQUIRED` — River Review does not make that call.

tasks.description: Task records as SUPPORTING evidence. At `final` scope, task exhaustion is explicitly NOT the completion criterion (`TASK_EXHAUSTION_IS_NOT_CONVERGENCE`), which is why 8-of-8 complete tasks cannot on their own produce COMPLETE.

complete.description: Tasks CLAIMED complete (e.g. a checked todo box). A claim is not a proof: see `unsupportedClaims`.

unsupportedClaims.description: How many of the claims in `complete` are unsupported. MUST equal `unsupportedClaims.length`; `tests/completion-assessment.test.mjs` pins the equality because JSON Schema cannot compare a count against an array length.

An unsupported completion claim: something declared DONE whose declaration is the only evidence for it. `claimSource` records what the declaration was; `missingEvidence` records what would have had to be present. A claim whose only `claimSource` is `todo-checkbox` can never support COMPLETE, which is the mechanical form of "Task DONE must not depend on a todo checkbox alone".

unresolvedRefs.description: Requirement / acceptance-criterion identifiers that could not be resolved to evidence. A non-empty list forbids COMPLETE.

evidence.description: What evidence was available for this assessment, one entry per kind. Absence is recorded rather than skipped: a `missing` entry is itself part of the answer and forces the state away from COMPLETE. JSON Schema draft 2020-12 は「あるプロパティでの一意性」を表現できないため、kind の一意性は tests/completion-assessment.test.mjs が強制する。

humanJudgment.description: The human boundary. Required when `state` is `HUMAN_JUDGMENT_REQUIRED`, and never a permission to proceed: it names the question River Review refuses to answer.

blockedBy.description: Why the assessment could not be carried out. Required and non-empty when `state` is `BLOCKED`.

allOf.title: task scope: no goal validation, task evidence required
final scope: the goal is the subject, so validation and requirements are required
COMPLETE requires zero unverified, zero violated, zero unsupported claims and zero unresolved refs
COMPLETE at final scope additionally requires the goal to be validated as met
missing or unreadable evidence forbids COMPLETE
COMPLETE requires diff and test evidence to be present, never a claim alone
HUMAN_JUDGMENT_REQUIRED must name the boundary it hands back
a goal needing human judgment cannot be recorded as anything else
BLOCKED must say what blocked it
an unsupported claim must be reflected in the state

then.description: #2019 AC: evidence 欠損は UNVERIFIED へ倒す。`INCOMPLETE` は「調べた結果 満たしていない」であり、`missing` は「調べられなかった」なので別物。両者を同じ状態で表すと、未検証を検証済みの否定として読ませてしまう。BLOCKED と HUMAN_JUDGMENT_REQUIRED は「そもそも判定に到達していない」点で UNVERIFIED と同じ側にあるため許す。

artifactRef.description: Identifier of a requirement, acceptance criterion or task as it is written in the source artifact (e.g. `REQ-7`, `AC-12`, `TASK-3`).

completionScope.description: Which question this assessment answers. `task` = "is there evidence to declare THIS task DONE" (Flow `task-completion-review`, intent `task-completion`). `final` = "were the goal and the requirements met", where finishing every task is explicitly not the criterion (Flow `final-review`, intent `final-convergence`). The two are separate semantics, not two thresholds of one scale: only `final` validates a goal, and only `task` requires task records.

completionState.description: The DONE state. Deliberately disjoint from GATE_DECISIONS (`GO` / `GO_WITH_OBSERVATION` / `NO_GO` / `ESCALATE`): a completion state is a statement about evidence, never an instruction to a host. `UNVERIFIED` is the fail-safe landing spot for absent evidence — an unproven claim is never COMPLETE and never silently INCOMPLETE either, because "we could not check" and "we checked and it is not done" are different answers.

validationState.description: Goal-level answer, used only at `final` scope.

completionReasonCode.description: Closed vocabulary explaining a completion state. Disjoint from GATE_REASON_CODES; the disjointness is pinned in `tests/completion-assessment.test.mjs` against the imported ledger rather than restated here.

evidenceKind.description: Kinds of evidence a completion judgment can rest on. `tasks` is listed so its ABSENCE can be recorded, not so a task record can stand in for proof.
